notes.ocean_floor.share_*: Erosion plan C4. terrain.ocean_depth_refinement gives every sea cell the depth at its area-weighted rank of the tectonic engine's depth on this curve, so the engine's ordering of depths stays (which sea cell is shallower than which; cells of equal engine height take the share at their group's middle) and the share of the ocean in each depth band is Earth's at every grid width and engine duration. Percent of the ocean area per band: ETOPO 2022 at 2048 columns, the hypsometry reference's inputs, as scripts/evaluation/landscape_statistics.py ocean-depths measures them (0-0.2 km 6.9, 0.2-1 4.5, 1-2 4.4, 2-3 8.5, 3-4 22.5, 4-5 32.1, 5-6 20.2, over 6 0.9; mean 3702 m, median 4104 m). Depth is linear in the area share within a band. The shares are normalised by their sum.
notes.ocean_floor.deepest_m: The lower end of the last band (over 6 km): the curve's deepest floor; trenches below it are made by terrain.tectonic_trenches.
notes.ocean_floor.minimum_depth_m: Every sea cell stays at least this far below sea level, the floor the earlier refinement kept on shelves (10 m).
notes.ocean_floor.texture_sd_m: terrain.texturing adds to sea cells its fractal normalised to zero mean and unit standard deviation times this, so the texture neither shifts the ocean nor grows with the grid width (the earlier 0.14 x (fractal - half the maximum elevation) lowered the sea floor by 0 to 4.6 km, because the fractal's draws cover only the lower half of the engine's 0 to 65536 m range, and its spread grew with the grid height in cells). 150 m: of the order of abyssal-hill relief (rms heights of order 100 m, Goff and Jordan 1988), a choice of order rather than a fit; it moves at most 1.5 points of ocean area between neighbouring bands at 128 and 256 columns.
notes.ocean_floor.smoothing_*_radius_km: terrain.smoothing averages each sea cell over a square of this half-width (land included), chosen per cell between the two by a fractal; the radius in cells is the radius in km over the cell size (the planet's radius x pi / rows), rounded, and 0 leaves the cell. The earlier radius was fractal / (maximum elevation / 6) cells, at least 1: nominally up to 6, but with the same fractal whose draws cover only the lower half of its range it was mostly 1 to 3 cells at every width (313 to 940 km at 128 columns). 20 and 120 km are a choice: 1 and 6 cells of the 2048-column world the stage was written for (19.5 km per cell). Cell sizes (6371 km radius): 312.7 km at 128 columns, 156.4 at 256, 78.2 at 512, so there is no sea smoothing at 128, 0 or 1 cell at 256 (1 where the radius reaches 78.2 km) and 0 to 2 cells at 512.
notes.ocean_floor.coast_smoothing_radius_km: terrain.coastline_adjustment averages the sea cells within this distance of a coastal sea cell over the sea cells within this distance of themselves (great-circle discs of cell centres, T8 W2-T2; earlier squares of the km over the cell size, rounded); the pull of the coastal cells themselves towards the coast depth is unchanged. 40 km is 2 cells at 2048 columns (19.5 km per cell). A disc of 40 km holds no other cell centre at 128 (312.7 km cells), 256 and 512 columns, so the smoothing acts from about 1024 columns. The marks that keep the sea cells within 2 cells of a coastal sea cell unshaded (presentation.no_shade) are set as before whatever the reach.
notes.texturing.land_scale: Terrain roadmap T2.2a. terrain.texturing adds to land cells this many metres per unit of its fractal's departure from the fractal's measured mean (the same mean the sea texture uses). The earlier term, 0.10 x (fractal - half the maximum elevation), lowered almost all land (mean -558 m at 256 columns, never more than +4 m), because the fractal's draws cover only the lower part of its range, and the floor at sea level + 5 m then held 81 % of the land area there. 0.10 is the earlier scale, kept. Since T8 W2-T1 the fractal is the sphere noise of terrain.sphere_noise.terrain_fractal_* and its mean is area-weighted over the whole surface (sea included), so land's area-weighted change need not be 0. The term is not normalised by the fractal's spread (the sea's is): the spread is now the legacy fractal's at 2048 columns (0.173 of the maximum elevation, about 8300 m) at every resolution, so the land texture has a deviation of about 830 m everywhere (before W2-T1 it grew with the grid height in cells and was smaller below 2048 columns; at 128 columns the land quantiles p75 and p95 went from 576 and 1092 m to 966 and 2017 m). The orchestrator's decision (2026-10-19): keep the 2048-column amplitude at every resolution; W3 recalibrates against Earth.
notes.sphere_noise.legacy_columns: T8 W2-T1 (docs/architecture/sphere-mesh.md sections 11 and 12). The terrain stages' pixel constants (stamp radii, distances between seeds, the warp's reach) and their counts per grid cell were written for the 2048-column world; on the cell grid a legacy pixel is the 2048-column cell at the equator, 2 pi R / legacy_columns km (19.5 km at R 6371), and a count per cell is a count per legacy cell, of which there are legacy_columns x legacy_columns / 2. Stamps cover the cells within that many km (mesh::cellswithin; a square box of half-width r pixels becomes a disc of radius r + 0.5 pixels), positions are drawn by area (mesh::randomcellbyarea), moves go through the tangent frame (mesh::tangentframe, fromtangent). So every resolution draws the same world in km: at 128 columns (312.7 km cells) most stamps cover only their own cell.
notes.sphere_noise.shortest_km: The shortest octave of every sphere noise below: the diamond-square fractals stopped at a step of two cells, 39 km at 2048 columns.
notes.sphere_noise.*_wavelength_km: Each legacy diamond-square fractal (createfractal, and warp's displacement fields) is replaced by landscape::FractalNoiseField at the cell centres' unit vectors (seed: the world seed and the caller's salt), octaves from this first wavelength down to shortest_km, each persistence times the last. Wavelength and persistence were chosen by the fractal's autocorrelation along rows at 2048 x 1024 (seeds as drawn, rows 256-768; T8 W2-T1 measurement): terrain_fractal (grain 8, valuemod 0.2 to 3-6: terrain.texturing, terrain.roughness, the volcano directions) d16 0.93, d32 0.80, d64 0.53 against 5000 km at 0.5 0.95, 0.85, 0.60; canyon_base (grain 16, 0.2) d8 0.73, d16 0.45, d32 0.16 against 1250 km at 0.6 0.76, 0.48, 0.10; canyon_mask (grain 16, 0.2 to 3-6) d16 0.87, d32 0.65, d64 0.24 against 2500 km at 0.5 0.83, 0.55, 0.12; archipelago (grain 8, 0.05) d16 0.87, d32 0.68, d64 0.35, between 2500 km (0.83, 0.55, 0.12) and 5000 km; warp_vary (grain 4, 0.002) d64 0.93, d128 0.74 against 10000 km; smoothing and warp as terrain_fractal. The rule of thumb is a first wavelength of the circumference over the grain.
notes.sphere_noise.*_mean: The legacy fractal's values, as a share of their maximum (the world's maximum elevation), per caller at 2048 x 1024 over four seeds: mean and standard deviation (terrain_fractal 0.358 / 0.173, canyon_base 0.423 / 0.252, canyon_mask 0.344 / 0.138, archipelago 0.408 / 0.224, warp_vary 0.335 / 0.109). The replacement is maximum x clamp(mean + deviation x z, 0, 1), at least 1, with z the noise's sum over its normalisation (unit deviation), so the callers' thresholds and scales keep the share of cells they had at 2048 columns, at every resolution. smoothing (0.5 / 0.2, not measured) needs neither for its scale: terrain.smoothing uses only the field's rank between its own extremes, so they only set where the clamp at 0 and 1 cuts (2.5 deviations).
notes.sphere_noise.warp_*: The legacy warp moved each cell's sample by (field / maximum - 0.5) x warpfactor x vary pixels east and south (warpfactor drawn from 20 to 80, vary the warp_vary field over its maximum); on the sphere the sample point moves by (clamp(mean + deviation z, 0, 1) - mean) x warpfactor x vary legacy pixels in km through the cell's tangent frame: the same spread without the legacy field's constant offset (its mean is not 0.5), which only translated the field.
notes.subgrid.spacing_coefficient: Multiscale plan S3.6. terrain.subgrid_statistics writes geosphere.valley_spacing = c x Lc, capped at the cell size (the square root of its area: a spacing wider than a cell means no sub-grid valleys, and a stored value equal to the cell size reads so), from Perron, Kirchner and Dietrich 2009 (Nature 460, 502-505: dz/dt = D lap z - K A^m |grad z| + U, n = 1; Pe = K L^(2m+1) / D = 1 gives Lc = (D/K)^(1/(2m+1)); first-order spacing 6.4 Lc to 12.7 Lc, independent of the erosion rate). The paper's five field sites give lambda / Lc of 7.0 to 9.5 (Table 1: Dragon's Back Lc 4.0 m, lambda 30 m; Point of the Mountain 7.5, 54; Napa Valley 13.7, 128; Gabilan Mesa 17.2, 163; Eaton Hollow 46, 321); 8 is a choice inside that range.
notes.subgrid.reference_*: Multiscale plan S3.6. The erosion's D and K are grid-scale values (with landscape.hillslope.diffusivity_km2_myr 200 and landscape.stream_power.erodibility 750, Lc would be about 115 km), so the valley spacing's D/K is calibrated to a site of Perron et al. 2009, Table 1, and varies from cell to cell as K_A does: D/K(cell) = reference_d_over_k x K_A(reference) / K_A(cell), with K_A = K x relative erodibility (geosphere.erodibility) x runoff^reference_m (discharge Q = runoff x area in the site's law K Q^m), so the ratio is (reference_erodibility / e) x (reference_runoff_mm_yr / runoff)^reference_m and Lc varies as runoff^(-m / (2m + 1)). Lc = (D/K)^(1/(2 reference_m + 1)) in m: the exponent of the site's fit. Default: Napa Valley, D/K = 86 m^(2m+1) at m = 0.35 (Lc = 13.7 m, lambda = 8 x 13.7 = 110 m), at 400 mm/yr of runoff (the reference runoff of landscape.stream_power.erodibility's derivation) and erodibility 1. A cell with no runoff or erodibility has no spacing (0).
notes.sphere_noise_coast.fine_*: T8 W2-T2 (docs/architecture/sphere-mesh.md sections 3, 11 and 12). The coast, shelf, ocean-feature, arid-landform and import functions use the terrain stages' legacy pixel (terrain.sphere_noise.legacy_columns), octaves (shortest_km) and fractals (terrain_fractal for the grain 8 fractals: shelves, ridge points, imported sea bed, land elevation, chains and craters; canyon_mask for the imported mountains' grain 16 radius fractal; warp_vary for the grain 4 trench fractal, the nearest measured set); a chance per cell is a chance per legacy pixel's area, 1 - (1 - p)^(A / pixel area). The fine group is the rough short-grain fractals the stages lack (createmountainsfromraw's peak heights, grain 256, valuemod 8; createoceanridges' regional displacement, grain 128, valuemod 4 to 8): first wavelength the circumference over the grain (about 160 km), persistence 0.7 for their large valuemod, mean 0.5 and deviation 0.25 (a choice, not a measurement: both functions run only from the desktop's import buttons).
notes.sphere_noise_coast.ridge_angle_deviation: createoceanridges blended each rift's crossing angle with a fractal of 1 to 360 degrees (grain 4, values wrapping); on the sphere the angle field is 360 x clamp(0.5 + deviation x z, 0, 1) of a warp_vary-shaped noise (terrain.sphere_noise.warp_vary_*), z of unit deviation: 0.25 clamps under 5 % of the cells to 0 or 360, so the field covers most angles in long smooth runs. Angles are relative to each cell's local east and north (sphere-mesh.md section 5).
